nonSensitive.heading: Loop promise
nonSensitive.content:
Loop will do its best to direct your feedback to any relevant organisations, and encourage them to respond. We will handle your feedback sensitively with the highest data security measures. If you share your contact details with Loop then we will let you know if anyone responds to your feedback. We will not share your contact details with anyone. 
Please note that we will remove any personal information that could identify you or others before publishing. The content of your feedback will stay the same, but identifying details will not appear to ensure privacy.

sensitive.heading: Your feedback is safe with us
sensitive.content: If your feedback is sensitive it will not be shared online, instead your data will be managed confidentially. A dedicated Loop case manager will contact you to get your informed consent and discuss options to try to get the right organisation to assist you with services or investigate your complaint. We can only do this if you share your contact information. We will not share your personal identifiable details or contacts with anyone without your permission.

sensitiveStory.title: What is sensitive feedback?
sensitiveStory.topParagraph: Feedback related to any of the following topics are considered sensitive:
sensitiveStory.bottomParagraph: If you share sensitive feedback, our moderators will ensure your feedback is handled in confidence. No personal identifiable details of sensitive feedback will be published online.

list.six: Breaches of an organization’s code of conduct or safeguarding policies

storyType.title: Type of feedback: your options
storyType.paragraph: You can categorise your feedback as one or more of the following types of feedback. Don’t worry though, if you leave it blank, a Loop moderator will tag your feedback for you. This helps us to try to find the right people to read and respond to you. We don't promise you anything, yet we will do our best to connect you to the organisations who should or could address your feedback.

thanks.title: Thanks
thanks.content: Show your appreciation for an organisation, a service, or someone in your community by writing feedback with a message of thanks

question.title: Request for Information
question.content: If you want to ask a question to an organisation, you can write feedback with a question in it.

suggestion_opinion.title: Suggestion / Opinion
suggestion_opinion.content: Do you have a strong opinion or do you want to share something you have heard about and see if it is true? Write feedback and tag it as an opinion.

request.title: Request for Assistance
request.content: Do you have an idea on how a service, or the work of an organisation could be improved? Write feedback and tag it as a request.

concern.title: Concern
concern.content: Are you worried or concerned about something in your community? Tag your feedback as a concern.

country.title: Why do we want to know the country you are in?
country.topParagraph: Knowing the country you’re in helps us understand the context of your feedback and to better understand patterns in each context to help with advocacy.
country.bottomParagraph: We automatically detect your country by using the IP address of your device. You can change or remove this country from your feedback at any time. Just click ‘Change country’

organisation.title: Why it is important to add an organisation to your feedback

sensitive.paragraph: Adding an organisation to your feedback helps us to know who can investigate your complaint. If you do not know the name of the organisation involved in your feedback, that's no problem. You can still submit your feedback without naming an organisation. However, we may not be able to assist you directly. Instead, it is possible that your feedback can be used for reporting and statistics, with your consent.

nonSensitive.topParagraph: Adding an organisation to your feedback helps us encourage that organisation to respond to you. It also helps us show which organisations are listening and responding to feedback through Loop.
nonSensitive.bottomParagraph: If you don’t know the name of the organisation involved in your feedback, that’s no problem. You can still submit your feedback without naming an organisation, and our Loop moderators will do their best to find an organisation to tag. Sharing more details helps Loop moderators find the right audience for your feedback.

name.title: Why do we ask for your name?

sensitive.paragraph: You can choose whether or not you provide your name. If you want to remain entirely anonymous, that’s fine as well. Simply leave the name field blank.

nonSensitive.topParagraph: Your name is displayed alongside your feedback, if it’s published on Loop. This helps personalise your feedback, and allows anyone who responds to your feedback to reference you by your name. You can give your full name, part of your name, or even a nickname.
nonSensitive.bottomParagraph: If you want to remain entirely anonymous, that’s fine as well. Simply leave the name field blank, and your feedback will be tagged as anonymous.

phoneNumber.paragraph: If you leave your phone number, Loop will keep you informed when answers will be published. Your phone number will not be visible to anyone and will never be published online.
phoneNumber.title: Why do we ask for your phone number?

email.bottomParagraph: Your email address is not published online, and we will never share your email address.
email.topParagraph: If you leave your email address with us, we’ll let you know when your feedback has been published. We’ll also let you know if somebody responds to your feedback.
email.title: Why do we ask for your email address?

age.paragraph: If you are younger than 14 years of age, you should ask an adult that you trust to help you fill out this form.
age.title: What if I am below 14 years of age?

condition.title: Why do we ask if you have a medical or physical condition?
condition.topParagraph: People who have a physical or mental health condition are often treated differently. If we know about this we can try to find an organisation that knows more about how to help you and better meet your needs.
condition.bottomParagraph: It will also help to advocate for funding and services to meet any gaps identified.

whatNext.title: What will happen next?
whatNext.topParagraph: Loop moderators will review your feedback. They’ll translate it, so that it’s understandable to as many people as possible.
whatNext.bottomParagraph: If you left your email address or phone number, we’ll let you know as soon your feedback is published online.

centerParagraph.part1: As long as your feedback doesn’t break the
centerParagraph.part3: it will be published within 48 hours.

whatHappenStory.title: What will happen to your feedback?

one.title: A moderator will read your feedback
one.content: Moderators read and translate all feedback coming into Loop. If the moderator agrees that your feedback is sensitive, they will send it to a Loop Case Manager. If the moderator does not agree that your feedback is sensitive, it will not be published. Loop will let you know why and what to do next if you leave your email or phone number. If you can only be safely contacted at certain times please leave that in your message.

two.title: A case manager will be assigned to your feedback
two.content: If you leave your contact details, the case manager will contact you to get your informed consent and discuss options to try to get the right organisation to assist you with services or investigate your complaint. We will also ask your consent to share any personal details such as your name, contact details, and location. You can choose at that time what to do.

three.title: We will try to get organisations to act
three.content: The Loop case managers will follow-up with any organisation involved in your feedback and encourage them to take action.

four.title: If we can contact you, we will keep you up-to-date
four.content: If you leave your phone number or email address, we will let you know when there are any updates on your case.

location.title: Why do we want to know the location of your feedback?

sensitive.paragraph: With your consent, Loop will use your location to identify services near you to assist you or to provide this information to organisations to support them to investigate your complaint. Loop does not gather your exact location.

nonSensitive.topParagraph: Loop uses your approximate location (for example the district or province you are in) to encourage organisations near you, to respond to your feedback.
nonSensitive.bottomParagraph: Loop does not gather your exact location. However, your approximate location will be displayed alongside your feedback. This helps us find the right audience for your feedback.

infoIcon.content: Understanding the response time for feedback gives us an indication of how engaged with community feedback we are as a sector.

If people share their demographic information with us, we aggregate it here. This helps us understand who is using Loop, and who we are not (yet) reaching. We can see what type of feedback they are sharing and the filters can refine this analysis further.

moreLink.content: When Loop receives sensitive feedback that would do harm if it was posted on the open platform we refer it to our trained Case Manager. Best practice requires all allegations to be acknowledged, assessed, investigated if appropriate, and the person making the allegation to be informed of the outcome. Each step of this process is reflected in this Accountability Process. To ensure a survivor centred approach sector standards state the time within which each of these steps should be completed by (see here). The Loop statistics page displays the data that organisations choose to share with Loop after receiving a referral. Organisation and Survivor/ Victim identifiable data is not disclosed here.

timeline.title: When are people reporting sensitive issues to Loop?

infoIcon.content: Sensitive issues reported to Loop are tagged as one of four categories. This graph shows the trends of when different types of issues are being reported to Loop.

accountabilityProcess.title: The accountability process
accountabilityProcess.description: From the moment a person submits sensitive feedback that proves to be an allegation, a Loop Case Manager reviews the allegation and processes the case accordingly. The responsibility of who has to act is tracked until the allegation is fully accounted for, the original author of the feedback has been informed, and the case can be closed. We call this The Accountability Process. It is designed to account for every allegation Loop receives, to create transparency for what happens to each resulting case, where it is being held up, and who is responsible to act.

moderatorReview.title: Moderator review
moderatorReview.description: The feedback is reviewed by a moderator and translated if needed. If it is sensitive, the moderator will forward the feedback to a case manager.

seeProcess.title: The step-by-step accountable process
seeProcess.firstParagraph: Loop is an independent charity, with the sole purpose of providing a safe mechanism for people to raise their voices to improve services at scale. As part of our duty of care we have developed a way to safely receive and refer on sensitive feedback that would do harm if they were posted on the open platform. This could include reports of Sexual Exploitation Abuse and Harassment (SEAH), fraud, corruption, protection issues or other forms of misconduct.
seeProcess.secondParagraph: We safely collect data (qualitative and quantitative) that people choose to share with us, we refer them on to appropriate actors to manage and to provide assistance where appropriate. We then reflect the data at an aggregate level for all to analyse and to identify trends, hot spots, pain points and where to improve.
seeProcess.thirdParagraph: Loop does not respond to sensitive feedback, investigate cases or write reports on the findings.  We are a reciprocal for engaging with hard-to-reach populations and for showing the trends of data on how different types of organisations are responding. Through this we hope to put the voices and experiences of local people on decision making tables.
seeProcess.fourthParagraph: We will adapt our tags and the Accountability Process to align with evolving best practice. We can only be as useful as the data that is shared with us.

1.title: A person submits sensitive feedback to Loop.
1.firstParagraph: Anyone can submit sensitive feedback using Loop: a survivor, witness, or an organisation. They share feedback at {{homeLink}} or the local SMS number and tag it as sensitive.
1.secondParagraph: The sensitive feedback will not be posted on the open platform, no one will receive identifiable or contact information about the author and high standards of data security are followed.

2.title: The feedback is reviewed by a Loop Moderator, identified as sensitive, and forwarded to the Loop Case Manager.
2.secondParagraph: Best practice requires all allegations to be acknowledged, assessed, investigated if appropriate and the person making the allegation to be informed of the outcome. Each step of this process is reflected in The Accountability Process.
2.firstParagraph: The moderator will send feedback which are tagged as sensitive to the Case Manager. They will also send feedback to the Case Manager if they believe it could do harm if it is posted on the open platform. We follow the Loop Protocols to define what is posted on the open platform and what is managed through the confidential secure case management system. You can read and help us improve these protocols {{hereLink}}.

3.title: The Case Manager reviews the sensitive feedback and refers on for immediate assistance, if needed.
3.firstParagraph: The Loop Case Manager is a trained specialist in handling allegations and complaints and refers the author of the sensitive feedback on to existing referral pathways. Loop does not provide assistance directly. We do provide a way for people to safely report, and we try to get this information to the best actor to take action. We can track assistance provided if organisations share updates with the Loop Case Manager.

4.title: The 'sensitive feedback' is now considered a 'case' and is entered into a process where each step must be accounted for in a timely manner before it can be closed.
4.firstParagraph: Cases are open until they have been fully accounted for in the Accountability Process. Cases are closed when no further action is required and where possible the author has been informed of the outcome. To ensure a survivor centred approach, sector standards state the time within which each of these steps should be completed.
4.secondParagraph: The Loop statistics page displays the data that organisations choose to share with Loop throughout the management of a case. Organisations, authors and Survivors identifiable date is never shown.

5.title: Process and refer.
5.firstParagraph: When Loop receives a sensitive case, Loop will process and refer it on to an appropriate organisation for 1) Accountability and 2) the provision of Assistance if needed. By sector standards, Loop is responsible to process and refer an allegation within 48 hours of receiving it. We track this information to see if Loop can deliver on this expected standard and to hold ourselves publicly accountable.

6.title: Response to referral.
6.firstParagraph: When an organisation receives a referral, it is expected, by sector standards, to acknowledge receipt within 48 hours. When Loop receives this acknowledgement, we will update the data. We track this information to see if organisations can deliver on this expected standard.

7.title: Decision to investigate.
7.secondParagraph: When an organisation receives a referral, it is expected, by sector standards, to assess and decide to investigate or not, within 6 weeks. If organisations inform Loop of this decision, we can update the data. Loop tracks this information so that we can all learn how long it takes to assess and decide to investigate or not, based on different filters/ parameters.
7.firstParagraph: To mitigate further risks and to protect people, an organisation is responsible to assess the information and establish if and how they will investigate the case.

8.title: Investigation closed.
8.firstParagraph: To encourage a timely and accountable process, Loop tracks all of these steps in the process, including the time it takes to close an investigation and the outcome.
8.secondParagraph: When an organisation opens an investigation there are many reasons why it can take a long time to complete. Loop keeps a track on this so that we can all learn how long it takes, on average, based on different filters/ parameters, to complete an investigation.

9.title: Author informed.
9.firstParagraph: A survivor centred approach, requires that, where possible, the person who submitted the allegation is, at minimum, informed of the outcome. If organisations inform Loop when they have done this, we can update the data. Loop tracks this data so that we can all learn if survivors/ victims are being kept informed or not. This is the last stage of the Accountability Process and a case then becomes a Closed Case and the data continues to be reflected in the overall data and filters.

infoIcon.content: Best practice requires all allegations to be acknowledged, assessed, investigated if appropriate, and the person making the allegation to be informed of the outcome. Each step of this process is reflected in this Accountability Process. To ensure a survivor centred approach, sector standards state the time within which each of these steps should be completed by ({{infoLink}}). This diagram shows the average time all cases are taking for each step of the process. If it is green it is 'on time', yellow is 'overdue' or red is 'unresponsive'. A closed case is when no further actions are required in the Accountable Process.

As per sector standard reporting, if organisations share with us the outcomes of referrals and investigations, Loop can show trends about what happened as a result of referrals. This helps us all to better understand the impact of individuals reporting sensitive feedback and organisations following an Accountable Process.

paragraph.main: Our overarching principle is that there is value in hearing a diverse range of views and that this powers greater impact. Therefore, we encourage all voices to be shared in a safe, supportive, enquiring manner. With respect for each other’s ideas, experiences, and viewpoints. We may not always agree, but disagreement is no excuse for poor manners. Be direct, constructive, and positive.
paragraph.1: Also, always assume the best. Understand that people may be engaging through different means and different barriers: Not using their native language; Coming from different cultures; Using pronouns other than “he” or “she”; Living in a different time zone; Facing other challenges to participate; not familiar with other social media approaches.
paragraph.2: The conversations we have here set the tone for every new arrival. Help us influence the future of this community by choosing to engage in discussions that make this forum an interesting place to be — and avoiding those that do not. Discourse provides tools that enable the community to collectively identify the best (and worst) contributions: tag in others, upvote comments, reply and flag to Loop any concerns or issues directly to help the community get the most out of the platform.
paragraph.3: To create a safe place to listen and engage, a moderator reviews all feedback or replies before they are posted on the open transparent platform. If contact details are given the person will be informed, by the moderator, of when it was posted or why it was not posted, and what they can do to correct it, so that it can be posted.
paragraph.4: We will not post feedback or replies for five main reasons:

paragraph.1: Loop aims to encourage people to engage safely and inclusively to listen to more voices. Therefore, we will not post feedback or replies which contain:
paragraph.2: Abuse or harassment: You may not engage in the targeted harassment of someone or incite other people to do so. This includes wishing or hoping that someone experiences physical harm, insulting or belittling them. It also includes sexualized comments or jokes in interactions.

1.title: The Feedback/ Reply has offensive or had discriminatory language in it.

2.title: The feedback / reply does not follow the community standards designed to ensure a safe space to share feedback.

paragraph.1: Loop can positively support data to inform improvements to service provision if more people from diverse backgrounds can participate to share, learn, and engage. We encourage new perspectives to be heard and listened to actively. Lead by example.
paragraph.2: Hateful conduct: You may not promote violence against, threaten, or harass other people on any basis, including: race, ethnicity, national origin, caste, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, religious affiliation, age, disability, serious disease, native language, socio economic status, geographic location, etc. Attacking someone for their opinions, beliefs and ideas is also not acceptable nor is derogatory or rude language
paragraph.3: Violence: You may not threaten violence against an individual or a group of people. We also prohibit the glorification of violence.
paragraph.4: Terrorism/violent extremism: You may not threaten or promote terrorism or violent extremism.
paragraph.5: Exploitation: We have zero tolerance for any form of exploitation, this includes child sexual exploitation.
paragraph.6: Suicide or self-harm: You may not promote or encourage suicide or self-harm.
paragraph.7: Illegal or certain regulated goods or services: You may not use our service for any unlawful purpose or in furtherance of illegal activities.

paragraph.1: Loop encourages people to speak in the first person about their own views and experiences, which maybe that someone else told them something. This will ensure that one piece of feedback represents one experience and one person’s view to ensure fair representation of views and experiences.
paragraph.2: Impersonation or False reporting: You may not impersonate individuals, groups, or organizations.  This can mislead, confuse, or deceive others.
paragraph.3: Platform manipulation and spam: Loop cannot be used for the purpose of manipulating or interfering in civic participation. This includes posting or sharing content that may suppress participation or mislead people about when, where, or how to participate in a civic process.
paragraph.4: Computer generated posts: You may not manipulate posts to reinforce a particular view or to sway opinion. Feedback and replies need to be true experiences from the individual posting the feedback and not speak for another person without their consent.
paragraph.5: Copyright and trademark: You may not claim to represent an organisation or person without their express consent.

3.title: There is a concern about the authenticity of the feedback / reply.

4.title: There is a concern that the feedback / reply could cause harm if posted publicly. It is being referred on to a specialist.

paragraph.1: Loop aims to Do No Harm to individuals and organisations as a result of Feedback or Replies.
paragraph.2: Protection: If, based on the feedback and other information voluntarily shared, posting the feedback on an open transparent site may jeopardise anyone’s safety in anyway, including potentially identifying them, then the feedback / reply will be returned to suggest removal of some identifying information or referred onto the sensitive feedback system. The Loop moderator may decide to remove some tags that the individual has disclosed if their is concern they can be identified and harm may result.
paragraph.3: Unconfirmed accusation: A post which contains a very inflammatory statement that could result in a significant risk to an individual or organisation will not be posted on the open site but will be referred to the Closed Loop service to be referred on to the appropriate actor to manage the information in a safe accountable manner.

paragraph.1: All posts must respect people’s right to privacy and confidentiality.
paragraph.2: Private information: You may not publish or post other people's private information (such as home phone number and address) without their express authorization and permission.

5.title: The feedback does not respect the right to privacy of others.

6.title: How to report if you believe that these Community Guidelines have not been respected:

paragraph.1: If however you feel that a piece of feedback or a reply has been posted that may breach any of the above standards or codes, please email hello@TalkToLoop.org with a link to the feedback / reply of concern and outline your perspective. You will receive a reply within 48 hours.
paragraph.2: In order to maintain our community, moderators reserve the right to remove any content and any user account for any reason at any time. Moderators preview all new posts; the moderators and site operators do as much as they can to keep a safe space, however we cannot take responsibility for any content posteby the community.
paragraph.3: We have used Twitter and Mozilla Rules and Codes of Conduct to inform this document. We will improve and update it as we learn and grow. Please share suggested edits and improvements.
